extra_misconceptions.fact: Work completed for another merit badge cannot be reused, so you must log a separate four-month period with counselor approval.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A four-month dog care log completed for the Dog Care merit badge also satisfies the Pets merit badge care requirement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: You must secure your merit badge counselor's approval before the four-month tracking window officially begins.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Prior months of feeding a family pet before meeting your counselor count toward the four-month care requirement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A dated log tracking daily feeding amounts, water changes, grooming, and expenses provides verifiable proof of consistent care.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A signed note from a parent at the end of four months is better evidence than a dated daily feeding and cleaning log.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Biofilm builds up on bowl surfaces within twenty-four hours, so water dishes should be washed with soap and hot water daily.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Refilling a pet water bowl each morning without scrubbing the inside keeps the drinking water clean and bacteria-free.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must a Scout obtain counselor approval before starting the four-month care log rather than counting prior months?
Under what condition does a four-month care record for a dog fail to qualify for the Pets merit badge?
What daily measurements in your care log help a veterinarian spot early appetite loss or dehydration in your pet?
Which sanitation steps during weekly enclosure cleaning prevent zoonotic bacteria like Salmonella from spreading?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many municipalities still enforce rabies vaccination, licensing, or household pet limits even for strictly indoor animals.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Indoor cats and caged pocket pets are exempt from all city or county animal ordinances because they never leave the house.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Guinea pigs cannot synthesize vitamin C on their own and develop scurvy unless fed stabilized guinea pig pellets and fresh greens.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Guinea pigs can eat standard rabbit pellets indefinitely because both animals are small herbivorous household pets.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Goldfish produce heavy ammonia waste and require at least a twenty-gallon filtered tank to prevent gill damage and stunted growth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A small round goldfish bowl provides sufficient dissolved oxygen and filtration for a common goldfish to live a full life.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ectothermic reptiles rely on external heat lamps or under-tank heaters to regulate body temperature and digest food properly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reptiles warm their bodies by absorbing heat from a thick blanket wrapped around the outside of their glass terrarium.

extra_socratic_questions: Where can a Scout look up municipal ordinances on rabies vaccination, leash rules, or exotic pet permits for their town?
What happens to a reptile or amphibian when its terrarium lacks a proper warm-to-cool thermal gradient?
What measurement confirms that a freshwater aquarium has completed nitrogen cycling before you add fish?
Why is it dangerous to line a small rodent cage with aromatic cedar or pine wood shavings?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Your reading material must be a book or pamphlet specifically approved by your merit badge counselor for accuracy and depth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any random social media post or unverified blog article satisfies the requirement to read an approved book or pamphlet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Veterinary literature notes that cats also purr when experiencing severe pain, fear, or distress as a self-soothing mechanism.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cats purr only when they feel completely relaxed and content in their surrounding environment.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A high, stiff tail wag paired with tense posture signals high arousal or agitation rather than friendly relaxation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A dog wagging its tail stiffly while holding its body rigid is always inviting a stranger to reach out and pet it.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All-seed diets cause vitamin A deficiency and fatty liver disease in birds; formulated pellets and fresh vegetables are required.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Parrots and other hookbills need only a bowl of commercial sunflower seed mix to meet their lifelong nutritional needs.

extra_socratic_questions: Why should your counselor review and approve your chosen pet book before you rely on its medical or dietary advice?
Which physical indicator in your reading distinguishes normal species behavior from early signs of illness or stress?
What enclosure dimension or dietary ratio from your reading caused you to adjust your pet's current home setup?
Why is it dangerous to give human pain medications like ibuprofen or acetaminophen to a dog or cat?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Long sessions cause mental fatigue and frustration, whereas five-minute sessions with high-value rewards build reliable habits.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hour-long daily training marathons teach a pet three new tricks faster than short five-minute sessions.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Delayed rewards reinforce whatever the pet is doing at the moment the treat arrives, so markers must happen within one second.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Delivering a food treat ten seconds after a pet completes a trick still teaches the animal which action earned the reward.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Any animal motivated by food can learn target touches, spins, or obstacle navigation through positive reinforcement and shaping.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Non-canine pets like cats, rabbits, rats, and aquarium fish cannot learn tricks because they lack a pack hierarchy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Aversive corrections make pets hesitant to offer new behaviors and can trigger defensive aggression or fear in a show ring.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Punishing a pet for making a mistake during trick training speeds up learning by eliminating wrong guesses.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must a clicker or verbal marker occur within one second of the desired action during pet trick training?
Under what condition should a trainer fade out the food lure and rely on a hand signal or verbal cue alone?
What session length and success percentage indicate your pet is ready to practice a trick with added distractions?
Which physical indicator at a noisy pet show tells you your animal needs to return to a quiet carrier immediately?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Credentialed veterinary technicians must graduate from an accredited program and pass the VTNE exam, unlike unlicensed assistants.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Veterinary technicians and veterinary assistants hold the same state license and perform identical medical duties.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Licensed veterinarians are trained and authorized across multiple animal species, from household pocket pets to livestock and zoo fauna.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Doctor of Veterinary Medicine is legally allowed to diagnose illness, prescribe drugs, and perform surgery only on dogs and cats.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Shelter professionals handle infectious disease isolation, behavioral assessments, record keeping, and compassionate owner counseling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Animal shelter workers spend their shifts playing with healthy puppies rather than managing quarantine and sanitation protocols.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Responsible breeding as an avocation requires costly genetic health screenings, emergency obstetric care, and lifelong return guarantees.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hobbyist pet breeders consistently earn high profits because purebred litters require minimal veterinary testing or care.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must a Scout get parent or guardian permission before interviewing a veterinarian, breeder, or shelter director?
Which clinical duties may a licensed Doctor of Veterinary Medicine perform that a veterinary technician cannot?
What tuition and licensing costs must an aspiring veterinarian weigh against median starting salaries in private practice?
Why is it dangerous to restrain an anxious animal in a veterinary clinic without species-specific fear-free handling gear?
